discrepancies.what: The stated percentage reduction in column 5 does not follow from the two ppm columns beside it in any row on this page, and it is not monotonic against the residual it is supposedly computed from.
discrepancies.drawing_says: As printed on this page: batch 3 reads 1327, 92, 74%; batch 4 reads 1327, 88, 89%; batch 5 reads 1327, 72, 91%; batch 6 reads 1327, 45, 98%. Computed from the two printed ppm columns, the reduction would be 93.07% for batch 3, 93.37% for batch 4, 94.57% for batch 5 and 96.61% for batch 6. The 93.07 / 93.37 / 94.57 / 96.61 figures are computed here for comparison only and appear nowhere on the page. Worse than the size of the gap is its direction: batch 3 has MORE residual cyanide than batch 4, 92 ppm against 88 ppm, yet prints a much lower reduction, 74% against 89%, so the printed column cannot be a reduction computed from the printed residuals.
discrepancies.text_says: Nothing on this page. The header row and the Table 1 caption are printed on p05; per that header, supplied by the coordinator, column 3 is the original cyanide impurity content in ppm, column 4 is the cyanide impurity content after treatment in ppm, and column 5 is the percentage reduction in cyanide impurity content. Recorded, not resolved: no printed cell was altered, and no cell was filled with a computed value.
